newsitem.title: USA: Dow rises to record, dollar also gains.
newsitem.headline: Dow rises to record, dollar also gains.

text.p: Stocks rose modestly Friday, pushing the Dow Jones industrial average to a record. Bonds and the dollar also rose.

Blue-chip stocks gained as investors snapped up big, well known issues before the year-end. The 30-share Dow average rose 14.23 points to 6,560.91, topping the previous record of 6,547.79 set on Nov. 25. For the week, it added 76.51 points.

In the broader market, gainers beat losers 1,495 to 936 on New York Stock Exchange volume of 252.5 million shares -- the quietest full session this year. That distinction had been held by Thursday's session, when 253.4 million shares traded.
Friday's gains extended the Dow's rally to its eighth consecutive session.
Technology stocks came under pressure, however, after software company Computer Associates warned of lower-than-anticipated revenues.

"Computer Associates almost stopped the Santa Claus rally. Technology stocks are coming under some pressure, particularly the software issues," said A.C. Moore, senior investment strategist at Dunvegan Associates.
The technology studded Nasdaq Composite index fell 3.19 to 1,291.38. For the week it gained 2.82 points.

Stocks received support from stronger bond prices. The benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 20/32, or $6.25 per $1,000 face value. Its yield, which moves in the opposite direction to the price, fell to 6.54 percent from 6.59 percent Thursday.

Bonds rose on an unexpected 1.6 percent drop in November orders of durable goods. It was the first decline in orders for big-ticket items in three months and stood in contrast with a 0.1 percent rise expected by Wall Street.
The dollar rallied again against the yen as concerns about a weak Japanese economy and stock market battered the country's currency.

The dollar surged as high as 116.20 yen around midday, its highest rate since March 31, 1993, before settling at 115.30. The dollar closed at 114.95 yen on Thursday after touching its highest level in 44 months.
The British pound surged against the dollar, ending the day at $1.6945, its highest level since October 1992, and well above Thursday's close of $1.6740.
In commodities pits, frozen orange juice prices fell sharply on forecasts for spring-like weather in Florida, bolstering prospects for a bumper orange crop.
The actively traded March juice contract lost 4 cents to 81.85 cents a pound. The January contract fell 4.30 cents to 78.10 cents a pound after hitting a low of 78.00 cents.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index fell 1.5 points to 4,091.0 and Tokyo's Nikkei 225 index rose 77.46 points to 19,369.04.
